editorial.headline: Cocoa Processing With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10731 covers the industrial processing of cocoa beans into core cocoa ingredients, with registration open across every listed business scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10731 is the cocoa-processing lane: the transformation of cocoa beans into cocoa powder, cocoa butter, cocoa fat, cocoa oil, cocoa paste, cocoa cake, and other cocoa products. The emphasis is on processing, not merely trading or packaging. It is the activity code for businesses whose economic substance sits inside the conversion of raw cocoa into the intermediate and finished cocoa materials used further along the food and manufacturing chain.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the code is not framed only for large industrial plants. A small producer and a larger processor may both sit within the same activity definition, provided the registered business is genuinely carrying out the cocoa-bean processing described in the scope. That breadth matters because the code follows the activity, not the glamour of the product or the size of the brand around it.

Nationally, the record is direct: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. Put simply, foreign ownership may reach the national ceiling of 100%. There is no partial foreign-ownership cap in this slim record, and no additional national condition is stated here. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, so the editorial conclusion must stay narrow: for this record, the national position is open to foreign ownership up to the listed ceiling.

The Bali picture is not a hidden closure. At the Bali level, the record records l4_bali_blocked as false and assigns the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Its reason is precise: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; this activity is not marked as blocked under that rule. So the honest reading is clean: nationally open, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the data provided.
